structured_output.summary:
The tree is out of date and its keep rules have drifted. E049 is now the tip (5.20 s), but H1, H2 and H4 still describe E036. E049 was kept on a +0.035 pp, 20-seed difference against a baseline from another build, which breaks H4's own gate (≥0.7545, same build). Its time margin (−2.07% against a 2% bar) is also inside E036's 5.29–5.34 s rebuild spread. The same thing happened at E027, which was kept below its 0.7535 rule, and the thresholds have moved from 0.7535 to 0.752, then 0.7545, then 'within 0.03'.

A repeated pattern undermines many refutations. Each tip is kept on a seed set, and then every challenger loses about 0.2 pp on that same set: after E017 (E022, E025, E030, E032), after E036 (E040, E041, E042), and after E049 (E052, E053). So several 'local optimum' and 'refuted' claims may only show that those changes are flat. Seeds 13–32 are no longer unselected.

E050 showed that every code change rebuilds and redraws kernels, so the 'same-build baseline' requirement can never be met. Nobody has measured how much a rebuild moves a 20-seed mean, and that number sets the noise floor for every decision since E044.

Some results contradict the tree:
- E047 shows group-3 convs run as efficiently as group 2, which undercuts H1.7's 'cheap capacity' premise; widening group 3 would cost about +6–7%, not ≤2.5%.
- E048, E052 and E054 break seed 1's 'persistent, init-tied' deficit.
- E054 contradicts H5.2's corollary that cutting per-step cost at a fixed step count is cheap.
- E054's −0.48 pp from halving stem updates is surprising enough that it needs an implementation check before it closes a branch. So does E051's −1.1 pp from one stem implementation.

Large axes were never tried: batch size since E006, plain EMA, LS 0.1, Muon lr ×2, ReLU, a larger 32 px share, and a plain re-measure of the epoch dial on the tip. The H1.5.4 code read and the H4.4.2 diagnostic are cheap and still undone.

The loop also discarded locally feasible, faster runs (E052 at 4.99 s, E053 at 5.07 s) using a gate that was never connected to the official 40-seed ≥0.75 bar. That policy should be decided explicitly.

critiques.issue: The keep rests on +0.035 pp (0.7539 vs 0.7535) on seeds 13–32, where the SE of the difference is about 0.08 pp. The E036 baseline was not re-run: it is the 0.7535 from E044's instrumented k0 copy, a different build, even though H2.6.9 required the same build session. The time criterion (≥2% below E036) passed at −2.07% against 5.31 s. E036 has read 5.29–5.34 s across rebuilds, so against 5.34 the saving is −2.6% and against 5.29 it is −1.7%. Both halves of the decision rule sit inside noise. E049 also fails H4's gate (20-seed mean ≥0.7545), and no override was logged.
critiques.suggestion: Change H2.6.9's verdict to 'supported, within noise (tie)'. Log the H4 gate override explicitly. Treat E049 as 'about equal to E036, about 0.1 s faster', not as dominating it. Before the next keep, re-run E049 on fresh seeds and rebuild it once to check that the time saving holds.

critiques.target: H4 gate and keep-rule drift (E027, E033, E034, E049)
critiques.issue: The pre-registered thresholds have moved toward whatever each result was. E027's rule said held-out ≥0.7535; it read 0.7526 and was kept anyway. E033's rule was loosened to ≥0.752. E034 and H4 set ≥0.7545 'fixed from now on'. E049 was then kept at 0.7539 under a new rule, 'within 0.03 pp of E036'. The rule H4 says must come first ('margin should be bought (H4.2.6) before any further time cut') was skipped: E049 is a time cut, and H4.2.6 was never run.
critiques.suggestion: Freeze one gate and write down why it has that value. Derive it from P(local 3-seed ≥0.753) and P(official 40-seed ≥0.75) under the measured build and seed noise. Then re-audit every keep since E027 against it, and record each override in the notebook with its reason.

critiques.issue: Seeds 13–32 have now driven decisions in E044, E045, E046, E048, E049 and E051–E054. E049 was kept on them, and every later challenger (E052 −0.21, E053 −0.24) is measured against E049's draw on the same seeds. This is the same structure as the E038 winner's curse the tree already worries about.
critiques.suggestion: Retire 13–32 as a held-out set. Run the E049 tip and the next challengers on fresh seeds 33–52. Re-score E052 and E053 there as well, because both were locally feasible.

critiques.target: Systematic 'challenger loses ~0.2 pp right after a keep' pattern (H1.3, H1.5, H1 'no booster has held up')
critiques.issue: E022 (−0.24 vs E017), E025 (−0.27), E030 (−0.24) and E032 (−0.23) were all measured against a baseline that had just been kept on the same seeds 3–12. E017's 0.7577 was itself the reason E017 was kept, and E022 is only −0.11 against E016. E040, E041 and E042 (−0.20 to −0.28) repeat the pattern against E036's 3–12. Almost every booster reads negative, which points to an upward-biased baseline more than to harmful changes. 'Local optimum on both sides' (H1.3) and the LS-regularizes-the-average mechanism rest on single 10-seed runs of about 2σ against biased baselines.
critiques.suggestion: Downgrade H1.3's 'local optimum', H1.3.8's mechanism and H1's 'no booster has held up' to 'no gain of ≥0.25 pp detected; may be flat'. Re-test the two cheapest boosters (Lookahead interval 10, LS 0→end) paired against a fresh-seed baseline before treating the averaging and LS branch as closed.

critiques.issue: E050 showed that removing cudagraphs does not remove rebuild variance. Every commit therefore gets its own autotune draw, and a same-build comparison between two commits is impossible. Nobody has measured how a rebuild moves a 20-seed mean. If the per-seed shifts (0.1–0.44 pp) are correlated, which the 0.35 pp spread in the 3-seed mean suggests, the 20-seed mean could move about 0.1–0.2 pp from build alone. Every decision since E044 (thresholds of 0.03–0.15 pp) would then be under-powered.
critiques.suggestion: Before any further sub-0.2 pp decision, rebuild E049 twice in fresh processes and run each build on the same 20 fresh seeds. Report the between-build SD of the 20-seed mean and add it to the SE of every comparison. Consider also checking whether forcing deterministic cuDNN algorithm choice (benchmark=False plus a fixed algorithm) removes the spread at an acceptable time cost.

critiques.issue: The '10 of 11 runs' claim no longer holds. Seed 1 is highest in E052 (0.7587), and seed 0 is lowest in E048 and E054. E048 and E052 change only data selection and order, not init, yet seed 1's deficit disappears. That argues against the 'tied to init' story H4.1 favours.
critiques.suggestion: Recount over E036–E054 and restate the claim as 'seed 1 is low in X of Y'. Lower confidence in the init explanation. H4.1.6's split between redrawing the data RNG and redrawing the init is the right diagnostic, but drop the −0.15 pp 'bias' correction until it runs.

critiques.target: E054 (intermittent stem backward, −0.48 pp) and H2.6 'closes truncation before 75%'
critiques.issue: Halving stem updates over 40–70% of steps cost almost as much as freezing the stem completely from 60% (E037, −0.56). That is very surprising. Plausible artifacts: skipped steps leave the Muon momentum buffer (momentum 0.6) stale and unevenly weighted; grads may not be zeroed between variants, so stale grads get reapplied; or BN or Lookahead interact with the variant switching. The tree treats this as evidence about the biology of learning without checking the implementation.
critiques.suggestion: Before closing the branch, unit-test the alternating step offline. Confirm that group-1 params, grads and momentum are bit-unchanged across a detached step and that the next full step's update matches a reference. Treat 'refutes' as provisional until that check passes.

critiques.target: E051 (stride-2 stem conv, −1.1 pp) and H2.5
critiques.issue: This is one implementation tested once, and the loss is large enough (−1.1 pp) to look like a bug. Dirac or identity-style init on a stride-2, pad-0 conv is not identity-like, and replacing conv→pool changes where BN-GELU sits relative to downsampling. The notebook says this 'closes the stem-structure branch'. That overreaches.
critiques.suggestion: Record E051 as refuting only 'stride-2 conv with the current init'. If the stem branch is revisited, test conv→avg-pool, or stride-2 with init matched to the pooled conv, before closing it.

critiques.issue: The premise that small-map capacity is cheap per MAC is contradicted by E047, where g3 convs run at 220–270 TF/s, the same as group 2. By E047's numbers, group 3 costs about 6.7 ms of conv time per 32 px step. Going from 512 to 640 multiplies conv1 by 1.25 and conv2/3 by 1.56, roughly +2.4 ms plus fused BN/GELU, so about +7%, not ≤2.5%. E010's narrowing works out to about 1.4 s/pp, roughly the dial.
critiques.suggestion: Re-cost H1.7.1 with E047's per-layer table, and drop E021's 'sublinear scaling' as support, because E047 explains it differently. Expect about the dial's rate, so give it low priority unless it is paired with a time cut elsewhere.

critiques.target: H5.2 corollary ('cheap levers cut per-step cost at a fixed step count')
critiques.issue: E054 and E051 cut per-step cost at a fixed step count and lost 0.48 and 1.1 pp. E053 cut per-step cost and lost 0.24. The corollary holds only where a layer has already finished learning (stem after 75%, whitening after 20%).
critiques.suggestion: Restate it as 'cut per-step cost only on layers whose learning has finished'. Add a diagnostic that tracks relative weight change or gradient norm per group across steps, and use it to predict freeze points instead of running dose sweeps (E037, E042, E053, E054 each cost a full run).

critiques.target: E045 arithmetic and the dial rate (H4.2, H5.2)
critiques.issue: The E045 notebook says '+0.2 s for +0.135 pp is ~0.7 s/pp', but 0.2/0.135 ≈ 1.5 s/pp, and the discard reasoning followed from the wrong number. The dial rate itself is stale: it was measured before the freeze, when epochs cost more. E046 (−0.14) plus E049 (+0.035) implies +0.25 epoch ≈ +0.175 pp, about 0.7 pp/epoch, well above the 0.44 assumed. Both numbers rest on cross-build baselines.
critiques.suggestion: Run H4.2.6 now (epoch dial on the tip, fresh seeds, plus a rebuild-noise estimate). It sets the exchange rate that every keep/discard ranking depends on. Then re-rank E045's early small batch against the new rate.

critiques.target: Batch size: the largest untouched axis (H5, H5.1.x)

critiques.issue: No Lvl1 explains why time levers are cheap only early and only on low-resolution pixels. Early steps still matter (E041, E045), late learning in every group is step-limited (E037, E053, E054), but the stem after 75% and the whitening bias after 20% are free. H1 (sample efficiency), H2 (per-step cost) and H5 (batch) each cover one slice, and the layer-by-time learning schedule appears nowhere.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl1 along the lines of 'the binding resource is optimizer steps on layers still learning; time is saved only where a layer's learning has finished'. Give it a measurable Lvl2: per-group learning curves from one instrumented run. Use it to choose freeze and detach points and batch schedules, rather than running sweeps blind.
